document-write.description: Behavioural type for the document. "document" = Y.js markdown (default for all text). "workflow" = markdown with actionable workflow JSON fences; saving never executes buttons. "html" = self-contained HTML blob rendered as iframe (use for presentations, reports). "agenda" = Y.js + task sync for the user daily agenda. "conversation_agenda" = Y.js + task sync for a per-conversation agenda. "attachment" = file reference (no content; details in metadata). "table" = spreadsheet, rendered as a data grid; only for CREATING one or rewriting it whole (frontmatter schema + one pipe table with a leading _id column) — use the `table` tool for every partial read/write, because a partial write routed through here rewrites every row and destroys row identity.

Write mode. upsert=full replace (best for overview, strategy, meeting-prep, or ANY whole-document rewrite/restructure/dedup — pass the complete new content directly). append=add to end (best for canvas, research, chat history). patch=surgical edit for a SMALL, localized change only (read doc first, then replace old_string with new_string) — do not use patch with old_string/new_string spanning the whole document; that forces holding two full copies in context and will exhaust it on a large doc. Use upsert instead.

config-read.description: "list" — discover the user's AOPs (name/id/hasPlaybook/isNoOp/selectionProcedure/customAssignmentInstruction/orgAssignmentInstruction/effectiveAssignmentInstruction), optionally filtered by aopName. "load_full" — read the full PLAYBOOK.md for one AOP, plus its org-level playbook (`orgPlaybook`) if one exists, plus an `editMap`: every referenced subagent/resource and each inline PLAYBOOK.md surface, tagged with `source` (user|org) + `writeTarget`. To edit playbook behavior, write to a target's `writeTarget` — do NOT choose user-vs-org scope by hand. "load_sections" — read only the named sections of one AOP's playbook (and the same sections of its org-level playbook if one exists), plus the same `editMap` (requires `sections`).

systems-write.description: Defaults "user". "org" shares the server with every member of the organization (org admins only); a member's own connection of the same name still wins.

debug.description: "cron" fires exactly ONE named subagent in isolation (requires subagentName). "before_meeting" fires EVERY before-meeting subagent wired to conversationId — not isolated to one subagent, since Cedar has no isolated-single-agent before_meeting path today; this mirrors what a real meeting trigger actually does. "webhook" fires one registered webhook (requires webhookId) through the same dispatch path a real inbound POST or Slack-channel message would take — conversationless, so save-draft/save-slack-draft/task creation are unavailable to whatever it runs.

cron only. "user" reads the subagent from your own AOP; "org" reads it from the org AOP linked to your own AOP (you can only test an org-level agent your own AOP is actually linked to, never an arbitrary other org's).

run-sql.description: File format when `out` is true. Default jsonl (one record per line) — prefer it, because CRM text contains newlines and line-based tools miscount CSV rows. csv for spreadsheets.

conversation-read.description: Search method. "vector" = semantic similarity (default), for meaning. "fts" = exact keyword match (BM25), for a literal string — an order number, a URL, a name, or "Attachments" to find emails with attachments. Vectors blur exact tokens; use fts when the answer IS the string.
The CRM connection's providerId — get this from `config`'s `read-settings` action (sections: ["connections"]).

conversation-write.description: People: upsert value={people:[{id,...changes}]}; history: append complete new entries or update existing IDs in value={entries:[...]}. Omitted properties stay; arrays replace. New rows need all required data. replace=value only; patch=old_string+new_string only. Null/omitted never clears; "" clears.
Set only when the field description instructs a signal; follow its red/yellow/green rubric.
Type of event: "meeting" for in-person or video meetings, "call" for phone calls, "text" for text/chat messages, "custom" for any other interaction.

'reconcile' (default): re-derive fields + tasks from the events now on the deal — NO draft. 'full': re-run the whole on-event pipeline for one event (incl. drafting) to reproduce a missing output — requires eventId.

task.description: Scope: #all lists all open work user-wide, ignoring ambient conversation/date filters; recommendations default on. Follow nextCursor. For a deal inventory omit scope and set conversationId. #crm-approvals lists open CRM approvals user-wide. #today covers the previous 7 days through today; #overdue is before today without a lower bound. Date scopes use conversationId if supplied, otherwise user-wide.

How this task will be carried out: email, slack, linkedin or whatsapp. Only set it when the channel is genuinely part of the commitment — "reply to this thread" is an email by definition. For open-ended work like "follow up with Sarah", LEAVE IT UNSET: you do not know today whether that follow-up should be an email or a Slack message, and by the time it comes due a channel may exist that does not exist now. An unset channel is decided at execution, with better information; a guessed one is recorded as fact and biases whoever picks the task up.

Task type. Options:
- response: reply to an inbound email
- follow-up: outbound follow-up email
- post-meeting: post-meeting recap
- pre-meeting: pre-meeting prep
- reactivation: re-engage a stalled deal
- manual: general user-visible task
- calendar: calendar invite or placeholder to send
- crm-opportunity: create a new deal/opportunity in the external CRM. REQUIRED notes format: include provider (e.g. "hubspot"), accountId if known, instanceUrl if Salesforce, and the full conversation skill's opportunity-creation resource instructions so the chat agent has everything when the user invokes it.
- field-approval: proposed field value change pending user approval. REQUIRED notes format: JSON string {"fieldName":"<field>","value":"<value>","fieldLabel":"<label>","conversationId":"<id>"} — this is parsed by applyFieldChange when the user approves.

Task status: 'todo' if this is the next task to be completed in this conversation. Use status='done' when the intended task action has already happened. Do not use cancel-task for completed work.
When using cancelOlderThan: filter to only tasks created by this actor. Defaults to "agent" so user-created tasks are never accidentally bulk-deleted.

mail.description: Filter by direction. Use "outbound" for emails the user sent.

calendar.description: Which calendar mutation to perform. "create" needs summary/startDateTime/endDateTime/attendees. "update" needs eventId plus any fields you want to change. "delete" needs only eventId.

Which conference `wantsMeetLink` creates: `hangoutsMeet` (Google Meet, the default) or `zoom`, which Cedar mints on the user's own Zoom account and attaches to the event. Only set `zoom` when the user asked for Zoom by name; a user who has not connected Zoom gets an event with no video link rather than a failure.

notify.description: Deliver on a specific channel instead of the user's default. Leave UNSET almost always — the user picks where their notifications land. Set it (e.g. "email") only when the message argues for a channel, such as a long written report the user wants in their inbox. Not a retry mechanism: a failed send already falls back to email on its own.

draft-comms.description: OPTIONAL - The semantic category of this draft. Pass when you know the purpose: emailResponses = replying to an inbound email, scheduledFollowups = a scheduled or proactive follow-up, postMeetingFollowups = follow-up after a meeting, preMeetingPrep = pre-meeting agenda or prep email.
Task type for categorization. Use "response" for replies, "follow-up" for follow-ups, "pre-meeting" for pre-meeting prep, "manual" for general tasks.

linkedin-write.description: The user explicitly asked for a note on this connection request. Required whenever `note` is set; never set it to justify a note the user did not ask for.

send-user-feedback.description: bug: a Cedar tool or agent failed or behaved wrongly. confused: the user or agent could not tell how something works. feature_request: a capability that is missing. Default other.

chat-context.description: Entity kind to resolve. Only "conversation" is supported today.

delegate.description: Optional skill to pre-load in subagent (includes both chat and execution skills). Not typically needed for analyzer type.

Google Workspace access level for this run. Defaults to 'read' — the executor may list, read and export Drive files but cannot create or modify anything. Pass 'collateral-write' ONLY when the task is to author a new Google Doc, Sheet or Slides deck (e.g. collateral creation); it additionally allows create/copy/batchUpdate. Deleting a Drive file, emptying the trash and any sharing/permissions change are blocked in BOTH modes and cannot be enabled.
